note: Study skeleton paraphrased from the course scope (not verbatim College Board prose; unit numbers are our own sequencing, not official CED numbers). Skill codes are indicative: 1.x concept, 2.x/3.x skill.

objectives.statement: Identify key features of polynomial functions including degree, leading coefficient, end behavior, and zeros.
Construct and interpret graphs of polynomial functions from factored and standard forms.
Solve polynomial and rational inequalities and interpret slant asymptotes of rational functions.
Explain how exponential functions model growth and decay using initial value and growth factor.
Evaluate and rewrite logarithmic expressions using log properties to solve exponential equations.
Construct and interpret graphs of exponential and logarithmic functions including transformations.
Explain how the unit circle defines sine, cosine, and tangent for all real inputs.
Graph trigonometric functions and describe amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline.
Verify trigonometric identities and solve trigonometric equations over a given interval.
Explain how points and curves are represented with polar coordinates and convert between polar and rectangular forms.
Graph polar curves including circles, rose curves, and limaçons.
Explain how parametric equations describe motion with a shared parameter.
Graph parametric curves and eliminate the parameter to find rectangular equivalents.
Explain vector magnitude and direction and how vectors model displacement and force.
Perform vector operations including addition, scalar multiplication, and dot products.
Explain how matrices organize data and represent systems of equations.
Perform matrix operations and use matrices to solve linear systems.
Distinguish arithmetic from geometric sequences using explicit and recursive formulas.
Calculate finite sums and determine convergence of infinite geometric series.
